title: Philips FMV Demonstration Disc native pause/continue
symptom: The Play Control sample accepts Continue after a paused MPEG sequence, then enters the VMPEG firmware divide-by-zero vector before disc DMA and presentation can resume
expected: Continue resumes the paused MPEG sequence from retained state

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: CDFM pause gates CDIC sector delivery with DBUF while the optical position advances; stop commands $23/$24 finish the sector under the head, and SS_Cont starts a new $2A read.
supporting_evidence: Philips play_control.c calls mv_continue followed by ss_cont.
The CD-i 220 cdapdriv firmware at approximately $429e0a writes the stop operation during SS_Pause.
CDIC_BlackBoxAnalyzer e861f76 test_mode2_read_stop_read measures DBUF $0000 pausing delivery, DBUF $4000 resuming at the advanced optical position, and stop completing the in-flight sector.
contradicting_evidence: Correcting this transport behavior exposed, but did not itself remove, the VMPEG firmware divide-by-zero on Continue.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: A hardware trace in which DBUF gating resets the configured mode or stop discards the sector already under the head would contradict this model.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: Native fmvdrv reads separate 16-bit decoded-picture and display-period registers at $E040A8 and $E040AA. The emulator left $AA zero, so Continue divided by zero at VMPEG firmware $E536B0 instead of comparing the decoded cadence with the player display cadence.
supporting_evidence: The failing trace reaches vector $0014 at VMPEG firmware $E536B0, whose DIVU.W operand is $AA(a3) with a3=$E04000.
The VMPEG firmware reads $A8 and $AA independently.
A 45 kHz display clock gives $0708 for PAL/25 Hz and $05DC for NTSC/30 Hz; the pinned MiSTer study reference uses those same externally visible values.
Programming $AA from the configured player standard removes the exception and allows DMA and presentation to resume.
contradicting_evidence: The available Motorola scan does not label these VMPEG-specific register offsets, so the register meaning is reconstructed from firmware behavior and corroborating implementation evidence rather than a primary register table.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: A hardware register trace showing a different $AA cadence, or a native Continue trace that never reads $AA, would require revising the model.

context.scenario: FMVDemo Play Control native Pause then Continue

experiments.strategy: Drive the title's own controls, retain pause and continue milestones, and require DMA and presentation counters to advance after Continue.
assumptions: The on-disc Play Control path is representative of native CD-RTOS pause/continue.
experiments.expected: DMA and presented-frame counters advance after Continue with no decoder errors.
experiments.actual: Continue count reached one and VMPEG playing returned true, but DMA remained at 1,860,244 words and presentation at 535 frames; CDIC was idle on $24 and both FIFOs underflowed.
improvements: The unresolved pause path became deterministic and executable without commercial media.
experiments.evidence_quality: high: direct Philips sample source plus bounded native-title diagnostics

conditions: CD-i 220/Mono-I VMPEG using native CDFM pause/continue
invalidated_by: Changes to CDIC command $24, DBUF gating, CDFM/PCL resume, DMA2, or VMPEG continue semantics
repeat_when: Any invalidating dependency changes or primary command documentation is found

context.scenario: Bounded retries of Philips FMVDemo Play Control Pause followed by Continue

experiments.strategy: Apply the bounded retry allowed by TN 88, trace the first post-Continue exception, and inspect the VMPEG firmware operand and cartridge registers.
assumptions: TN 88 error 246 is a native pause race and does not by itself prove an emulator defect.
experiments.expected: A successful pause exposes the first emulator-specific divergence after Continue.
experiments.actual: Continue entered exception vector $0014 at firmware $E536B0 because the DIVU.W divisor in FMV register $AA was zero.
improvements: Separated a documented native E$NotRdy pause erratum from the emulator's missing timing register.
experiments.evidence_quality: high: native Philips title, Philips technical note, firmware instruction trace, and register state

conditions: VMPEG native fmvdrv pause/continue and other cadence comparisons
invalidated_by: A primary VMPEG register table or hardware trace contradicting the reconstructed $AA meaning
repeat_when: The DCLK basis, player cadence, or VMPEG register map changes

context.scenario: FMVDemo Play Control native pause/continue with PAL display period $0708

experiments.strategy: Program $AA as 45 kHz divided by the player frame cadence, preserve it across cartridge reset/power cycle, and require post-Continue DMA and presented frames to increase.
assumptions: PAL output is 25 frames/s and NTSC output is 30 frames/s for the firmware's display-period calculation.
experiments.expected: No divide-by-zero; DMA and presented video resume after Continue with no decoder errors.
experiments.actual: The gate passed. A paused milestone had 796,092 DMA words and 227 presented frames; after Continue the run reached 1,058,376 DMA words and 302 presented frames, with 304 decoded frames and zero demux/video/audio decoder errors.
improvements: Native VMPEG Continue completes and resumes the disc-to-DMA-to-decoder path.
experiments.evidence_quality: high: deterministic native-title gate plus firmware-level exception removal

conditions: VMPEG on PAL or NTSC Mono-I players
invalidated_by: Changes to DCLK timing, video-standard propagation, reset semantics, or the FMV register model

manual_verification.notes: User tested the PAL Philips FMVDemo Play Control panel in the release GUI. The title's on-screen Pause stops presentation and clears the transient horizontal slice; Continue resumes both video and audio normally. The slicing itself remains open as a separate presentation-timing incident.
